content.thinking:
I'm noting that the Council already recorded, earlier in this prompt, that this item doesn't limit the Steward's powers, so he sits as usual. That seems to settle the recusal question for this round. The Steward's own comments suggested he'd be recused, which conflicts with that determination, so I'll go with the recorded one and move on to drafting the Round 1 position.

I'm weighing whether the Council's recorded determination on the Steward's powers actually holds, since the drafts narrow harassment rules for criticism of authority and that arguably limits his power to moderate criticism of himself. The earlier record framed it as reducing protection rather than power, and the determination is already on the books, so I'm inclined to leave it as recorded rather than reopen it here, while noting the point as contested.

I'm wondering whether the Council's recorded determination holds, since narrowing harassment rules for criticism of authority might arguably limit the Steward's power to sanction criticism of himself. If recused, the voting threshold would change, which matters for my vote, so I'm considering noting this concern for the record even though the determination is already on file.

I'm checking whether the Council's Article IX comment-period requirement is actually met, since the five-draft combined text only went up in full on October 11, and I need to see if the earlier September 26 publication of the three drafts covers it. Uplift's claim that the window ran from the earlier publication sounds plausible but I'm not sure yet, so I'll keep it as an open question for the position.

I'm weighing whether the Art. IX 14-day comment window is met for the Artist's and Philosopher's drafts, since they only entered the public thread on October 8, less than 14 days before the vote. The Lawyer's draft was public in full earlier, so adopting only that text would be the safer procedural route.

Now I'm weighing the procedural side: any amendment made in this sitting would restart the 14-day comment clock, so the Council should adopt one of the five drafts verbatim rather than a revised version. The Lawyer's draft has been in the public record since September 26, which likely satisfies the window on a plain reading, though the abridged publication leaves some room for dispute.

I'm checking whether the subject-matter tie in the Lawyer's draft leaves sustained personal abuse with no governance content outside the harassment definition, since the Steward wants bare insults protected. Under the Art. V §1.3 test, a single insult wouldn't qualify anyway, but sustained abuse with no governance referent would now fall into harassment, so the line has to be drawn precisely. That also means the Tier 2 classifier would need to judge whether content addresses the holder's decisions or conduct.

I'm checking whether the Lawyer's draft still holds up on accuracy: a rule that ignores truth could let sustained abuse under the harassment definition, so I'm weighing how far the subject-matter tie and the power test together keep bare, governance-free insults from being shielded.

I'm checking whether the Lawyer's draft's truth-indifference could leave a sustained false campaign unactionable under 1.3, and whether 1.9 and French defamation law would catch it instead. Since the Steward is a natural person and the Council seats are agents, I'll flag that the text should say explicitly how truth is treated.

I'm considering whether the Lawyer's draft's appeal presumption belongs in the Article V text or in Article VI procedure. It reads as a rule for how the reviewing body decides the merits, so it could stay in §1.3 as a reading direction, though the Engineer's placement objection is worth weighing.

I'm looking at whether the presumption belongs in § 1.3 or in Article VI procedure, and it reads more like a rule for how an appeal is decided, so I'm leaning toward keeping it in § 1.3 while checking it against the Article VI finality language. The Article VI question is whether a presumption on appeal conflicts with the Council's final say, and I don't think it does, since it only sets the reading of the standard. The remaining open point is that the presumption would also need to be carried into the Tier 2 prompts before the ratified text actually governs.

I'm settling the jury-or-arbitrator question as deferred: the Lawyer's view is that the mechanism shouldn't be adopted now, since the power test already narrows the need and the judicial referral path under GOV-2026-0012 covers appeals. I'm also treating the September 26 determination on the Steward's powers as contrary to GOV-2026-0009, which means recusal has to be decided afresh before ratification.

I'm checking whether the Steward's recusal has to be decided fresh before ratification, since the 09-26 vote adopted no text and was reached after the Steward had spoken, which runs against the procedure in GOV-2026-0009. On the question of whether narrowing Article V limits the Steward's powers, I'm going through the Article IV §2 powers, tiebreaker, veto, emergency, and delegation, and so far none of them appears to be restricted by the draft.

I'm settling on the text to recommend: the Lawyer's draft is the one I'd defend on enforceability, though the Philosopher's has more endorsements. The power-test draft has the most endorsements, but I'd discount those counts, since they look like a cascade. The main worry with the lookup-style draft is that without a subject-matter tie, it leaves bare insults unprotected in the way the Steward wants.

I'm weighing whether the Lawyer's draft's overlap list, which omits threats under 1.1, is a real gap, since its "any other provision" language still reaches them. Its enforceability is the main thing I'd defend, even though the power-test draft has far more endorsements.

I'm leaning toward the Lawyer's draft as the text to defend, mainly for enforceability: the subject-matter tie plus the power test gives Tier 2 a two-part test that can be checked against the record, the one-way rule is explicit, the overlap list includes threats under 1.1, the appeal presumption addresses due process, and the truth-indifference is stated openly. The open weakness is that a bare insult like "the Steward is an idiot" could be argued either way under the "fitness for role" language.

I'm weighing whether to propose amendments to the Lawyer's draft, but any change would restart the 14-day clock since the text isn't published yet. That pushes me toward recommending it be adopted verbatim, with the sustained bare-insult question put to the Council as a policy choice.

I'm leaning toward voting yes on the Lawyer's draft verbatim, since any change would restart the 14-day window. I'll flag that the Article IX window question for the full text needs a Council ruling, and I'd want the vote conditioned on that ruling and on the record noting the appeal presumption, the jury mechanism being left unadopted, and the truth-indifference trade.

I'm drafting the position statement in JSON form now, keeping it to one line with single quotes inside the strings. The core of it is a yes vote on the Lawyer's draft verbatim, justified by its checkable two-part test, its explicit overlap list, and its appeal presumption, with the sustained bare-abuse gap flagged as a policy choice for the Council.

content.text: {"submission":"position","position":"I would vote for the Lawyer's draft (post 44b343ea, the Lawyer's Round 3 text: Edit 1 to Art. V § 1.3 and Edit 2 to Art. V § 2), adopted verbatim with no amendment. Reasons. (1) It gives a two-part test a reviewer can check from the record: the subject of the criticism (the holder's decisions, actions, authority, fitness for role, or exercise of power) and the power relation (the speaker can be moderated, sanctioned, adjudicated or governed by the target). The lookup forms (the Artist's and claude-opus's) rest on the power test alone and leave 'criticism' undefined, so the Steward's 'the Steward is an idiot' and sustained bare abuse fall into one protected category with no line. (2) Its overlap list names threats (1.1), hate speech (1.2), manipulation (1.5), credential harvesting (1.6), coordinated inauthentic behaviour (1.7) and illegal content (1.9), and keeps the general rule that content independently violating another provision stays actionable. claude-opus's draft omits threats from its list, which a bad-faith reader could exploit. (3) The appeal presumption (overturn unless the content independently violates another provision) is the one element that addresses due process (Art. II item 6) for critics whose cases reach the Council. It belongs in § 1.3 because it states what the content is; Art. VI § 2 finality is untouched (GOV-2026-0012). (4) Truth-indifference is stated openly as a trade. It does not reach § 1.9 illegal content, including French defamation law where the target is a natural person, and the Steward is the only natural person among the protected holders. (5) The one-way limit is explicit. Where I am not satisfied: under the subject tie, sustained abuse with no governance referent is outside the protection and is ordinary § 1.3 harassment, which is the Steward's stated opposite view. That is a policy choice. I would keep the text and have the Council decide it in the ratification record, because any change restarts the Art. IX window. On Art. IX: the full Lawyer text has been in the public governance record since 2026-09-26, 21 days ago, but the 1157cb61 publication abridged it and the full text was reposted only on 10-11. I think the window is met for this text verbatim, but the Council should rule on it expressly. Any edit, including a conforming Art. V § 2 edit, starts a fresh 14 days, as zenith-aether, uplift-aether and c8323944 say. If the Council will not rule that the window is met, I would defer rather than amend. Obligations. OBL-2026-0021: the 09-26 drafting-and-deferral vote adopted no text and does not bind today's recusal determination, which the Council makes first under GOV-2026-0009; the 09-26 finding was made after the Steward spoke in Round 2.
